newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Fed, Easter sideline issuers.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Fed, Easter sideline issuers.

text.p: Brazilian Eurobond issuers were expected to spend most of the week on the sidelines, awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve decision on interest rates and putting off new deals until after Easter.
Sour bond market conditions over the past two weeks -- fueled by rising expectations of a hike in U.S. interest rates -- have caused some issuers to re-examine the timing of their deals.

"Issuers and investors will stick to the sidelines. There's too much uncertainty until after Tuesday" when the Fed holds its FOMC policy making meeting, said a bond trader at a large international bank in Brazil.
Bond markets have already priced in a 25 basis point hike in short-term U.S. interest rates.
STATE-OWNED POWER FIRMS were expected to price deals once the short-term market trend becomes more clear following the Fed's decision and the long Easter weekend.
Sao Paulo state power company Cesp said it would wait until April to launch its $200 million 10-year, with five-year puts and calls. The deal, led by J.P. Morgan, was originally planned for March.

The Cesp issue, which will have no government guarantee, was expected to be priced at between 250-300 bp over the five-year U.S. Treasury. The firm's guaranteed 9-1/4 percent Mark due 2001 ZSED closed Friday at a spread of 270 bp.
seen pricing its $150 million eight-year, put-able at five, before the end of the month. A source at lead manager Santander said the new target date for the issue was mid-April.
Also, talk surfaced late last week about $300 million and $90 million deals by federally owned Eletrobras and power generator Furnas, respectively. Both bonds were expected to be issued by June.
THE BRADY MARKET was expected to pick up steam after Tuesday, even if the Fed raises interest rates by 25 bp.
"There is a lot of cash out there which will probably come back in once the Fed moves. The market just wants to get the Fed move over with," said one trader.
But Tina Vandersteel, a fixed income analyst for J.P. Morgan in Brazil, said there was some feeling in the market that a 25 basis point hike might not be sufficient.

"The risk is that if the Fed raises by 25 basis points, and numbers start coming in that continue to show expansion, then the market could start to think the Fed was behind the curve," Vandersteel said.

Under that scenario, the U.S. Treasury market could remain volatile, anticipating yet another 25 bp hike. Since investors tend to sell C bonds and other fixed-rate assets during volatility, Vandersteel said floating rate DCBs BRFLTD12=RR and NMBs BRNMB=RR might look a little more attractive over the next two weeks.

Still, traders said the more liquid C bonds look enticing at 77-1/8 or 450 bp over Treasuries, where they closed on Friday. Cs fell to as low as 380 bp over Treasuries in the latest rally and are expected to end the year in the 350 bp over range.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, Eurobond spreads have held out better than Bradys.
Brazil's global 8-7/8 percent due 2001 ZQ4P, which widened to 250 bp over Treasuries when the Treasury market fell two weeks ago, had tightened back to 210 bp over by Friday's close.

Although the global was not seen tightening much further, traders said a switch into the global and out of Petrobras 8-3/4 due 2001 ZPHN made sense. The Petrobras bond tightened to 130 bp over on Friday, making it very pricey compared to the sovereign issue.
Players also like Cesp's 9-1/4 percent due 2001 ZSED, which closed Friday at 270 bp over. The bond carries a sovereign guarantee and has traded as tight as 230 bp over recently.
((--Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
